Sandbox_DanTraitsAgeEnabled_tooltip:
Characters are in their 20s, 30s, 40s or 50s, which changes their starting skills, how fast the body recovers and trains, and how some traits work.
Off: the age traits are hidden and do nothing.
Sandbox_DanTraitsAgeDefault_tooltip: The age given to a character who has no age trait: a save from before Age had traits, or a character made without the creation screen. Rounds down to the decade: 20-29, 30-39, 40-49, 50-59. New characters pick their age on the creation screen.
Sandbox_DanTraitsAgeWants_tooltip:
Each age wants something every day, shown as a moodle, with a small reward for meeting it and a small cost for ignoring it. 20s: Itchy Feet (days in one place weigh on you; new ground lifts you) and slow mornings after an early rise unless there is coffee. 40s: a morning coffee and a meal at the usual hour each cheer you a touch. 50s: the same bed, a meal at yesterday's hour and a morning drink keep you right, three broken days put you out of routine; the cold bites more; a proper bed rests you more. Restless rides on Itchy Feet.
Off: none of it, and Restless does nothing. The ages' own effects (levels, recovery, the head) are not touched by this switch.
Sandbox_DanTraitsAgeBonus20s_tooltip: Levels a new character in their 20s gains (above 0) or loses (below 0) in their profession's main skill. -2 by default: the young start barely trained, and the profession's other skills lose one each. Nothing goes below level 0, and the profession's XP bonus is kept. 0: no change. A save made before this default was -2 keeps its old value.
Sandbox_DanTraitsAgeBonus30s_tooltip: Extra levels a new character in their 30s gets in their profession's main skill (Maintenance for the Unemployed).
Sandbox_DanTraitsAgeBonus40s_tooltip: Extra levels a new character in their 40s gets in their profession's main skill (Maintenance for the Unemployed). Above 0, the profession's other skills get one level each.
Sandbox_DanTraitsAgeBonus50s_tooltip: Extra levels a new character in their 50s gets in their profession's main skill (Maintenance for the Unemployed). Above 0, the profession's other skills get two levels each.
Sandbox_DanTraitsBloodEnabled_tooltip:
Bleeding drains blood instead of health: pale, then light-headed, then shock. Blood comes back with water, food and rest. An open wound still hurts the body part (see Wound Damage).
Off: vanilla bleeding.
Sandbox_DanTraitsWoundDamageEnabled_tool:
With Blood Loss on: an open wound also damages its body part until it is bandaged (a deep wound or a bullet left in until it is stitched or removed), as in vanilla. The neck and head count for most of your overall health, so wounds there show most.
Off: an open wound costs blood, not health (it can still go bad); bleeding takes health only once you are in shock.
Sandbox_DanTraitsInfectionEnabled_toolti:
Wounds can take an infection that grows: local, then fever, then sepsis. Clean and dress wounds early; once it spreads, only a course of antibiotics (a dose every eight hours) stops it.
Off: vanilla wound infection.
Sandbox_DanTraitsWoundExpansionCompat_to:
With Kaoeutsu's Wound Expansion loaded: where both mods model the same thing, this mod's version runs and Wound Expansion's stands down (its concussion, its torn and poorly placed stitches, its septic fever, its necrosis and sickness from an infected wound, and its own infection roll), each only while the system here that takes it over is on. Its dirty wounds and torn bandages count here (a filthy wound spoils the dressing over it and makes infection likelier), and its blood bag puts blood back.
Off: both mods run as they are, and double up.
Sandbox_DanTraitsWoundCareEnabled_toolti:
Dressings wear out and need changing, deep wounds heal slowly unstitched and can open again, fresh stitches can tear under strain, stitches and splints are put in with a First Aid roll, and walking on a broken leg makes it worse.
Off: vanilla wound care.
Sandbox_DanTraitsConcussionEnabled_toolt:
Hard falls, car crashes and blows to the head can concuss: headache, nausea, dizzy spells, light hurts; a bad one knocks you out. Rest heals it; a helmet helps. The headache can come back worse a day or two later.
Off: no concussion.
Sandbox_DanTraitsVitalityEnabled_tooltip:
Diet, exercise and sleep roll into a slow Vitality score: run down or thriving changes recovery, mood, health and how the traits behave, and Thriving gives half as much Fitness and Strength experience again.
Off: no score and no effects.
Sandbox_DanTraitsSleepLightEnabled_toolt:
Dark sleep is deeper and scores better; a bright room makes sleep shallow and light can wake you. Curtains and switches matter.
Off: light does not affect sleep.
Sandbox_DanTraitsSleepClothesEnabled_too:
Sleeping dressed is shallower sleep: you rest slower and the night scores worse. Underwear, socks, a T-shirt or shorts are fine. Warm clothes stop counting as it gets cold (free at 10C or below, or while you feel cold), so you never have to freeze; shoes, bags and armour always count.
Off: clothes do not affect sleep.
Sandbox_DanTraitsHomeEnabled_tooltip:
Where you sleep most nights becomes home after three nights there. At home boredom, stress and low moods ease, nights score better and books go faster; two days away and you miss it, until you are back. Homebody and Nomad change how much.
Off: no home is tracked and the two traits do nothing.
Sandbox_DanTraitsFitnessEnabled_tooltip:
Muscles tire and recover: training a rested group pays more, a sore one less. Pumped after a workout, Loosened Up after stretching, Overtrained after seven hard days in a row. Improvised weights, stretching, jogging, carrying and hard work count. Training plans and fitness magazines.
Off: training is vanilla's, nothing is tracked, and the magazines and Newbie Gains do nothing.
Sandbox_DanTraitsFitnessXp_tooltip:
How fast Fitness and Strength grow, in percent: every gain of either is scaled by this, on top of the mod's own bonuses (Ready muscles, plans, magazines). 100 is the mod as designed; 200 is twice as fast, 50 half.
Needs Fitness Training on. The game's own XP multipliers still apply as well.
Sandbox_DanTraitsFitnessStrain_tooltip:
Training a sore muscle group, or one group for too long, can pull a muscle: pain and stiffness, and that group cannot be trained for a day and a half.
Off: no pulled muscles; the rest of fitness training is unchanged.
Sandbox_DanTraitsCookingEnabled_tooltip:
A proper cooked meal (300 calories of a dish with two ingredients or more) leaves a Good Meal afterglow: low mood and stress ease for three to five hours, more for a better cook, more ingredients and spices, and at home. With Fitness Training on it also makes you Fuelled (Fitness and Strength experience +5 to 15%%) and adds one buff by what the dish is mostly: protein speeds muscle recovery, carbs spare endurance, fat keeps hunger off. Bulk and Cut diet goals in the fitness window.
Off: meals are vanilla's.
Sandbox_DanTraitsHangoverEnabled_tooltip:
Drinking past a buzz builds a hangover for the morning after: headache, low mood, thirst, tiredness, slower endurance recovery, and a worse night's sleep.
Off: no hangovers.
Sandbox_DanTraitsDrinkReliefEnabled_tool:
Drink eases pain and panic in proportion to how drunk you are, instead of one sip counting as a full dose of painkiller and beta blocker. Being drunk also drains unhappiness, stress and boredom, faster the drunker you are.
Off: vanilla, any drink is a full dose, and no mood lift from being drunk.
Sandbox_DanTraitsSunburnEnabled_tooltip:
Hours in the summer sun on bare skin burn it: a day of pain on each burnt part, and a worse night. Clothing, a hat, shade and sun block protect, and skin toughens with each burn.
Off: no sunburn.
Sandbox_DanTraitsDehydrationEnabled_tool:
Hours spent thirsty bring a headache, tiredness and slower endurance recovery until you drink.
Off: vanilla thirst only.
Sandbox_DanTraitsMedSideEffectChance_too:
The chance in percent, on each day a medication is taken, that its mild side effect shows up for a few hours. Taking too many at once is always harmful.
0: no side effects.
Sandbox_DanTraitsMedReminderMoodle_toolt:
A character on a daily medication for one of their traits sees a Medication Due moodle when the next dose is due, and Missed Medication once it has worn off.
Off: no reminder. The Medication button on the health panel still shows when each was last taken.
Sandbox_DanTraitsStartingMedication_tool:
Characters with a medical trait start with its medication: beta blockers (Heart Condition), anticonvulsants (Epilepsy), insulin pens or metformin (Diabetes), an inhaler (Asthma), baclofen and amantadine (Multiple Sclerosis), painkillers (Arthritis), and the last two tablets of a pack of sumatriptan (Migraines).
Off: they start with none and have to find it. Daily pills taken that morning still wear off over a few days.
Sandbox_DanTraitsArthritisWeaponDrop_too:
An arthritic grip that slips makes the swing land weak. In a bad flare (cold and damp), one slip in three throws the weapon to the ground.
Off: a slip only ever weakens the swing.
Sandbox_DanTraitsMSSpoons_tooltip:
Multiple Sclerosis: the spoons (units of energy) a full night gives. The day spends them by effort, faster in the heat or a flare; a bad night gives fewer, never under a third; a flare caps them at two thirds. At none you hit the wall, and every hour you push on is borrowed from tomorrow.
0: no budget. MS tires you a fifth faster instead, as it used to.
Sandbox_DanTraitsAngerEffects_tooltip:
The Angry moodle (a smoker's withdrawal raises it) does something, for everyone, from Annoyed up: melee weapons wear faster, reading is slower, splints, stitches and vehicle parts go wrong more often, and from Angry up the character curses out loud where zombies can hear. Furious also costs extra endurance per swing.
Off: the moodle is only for show, as in the base game.
Sandbox_DanTraitsSmokerCravingMoodle_too:
Smokers see a Nicotine Craving moodle and a notice when a craving starts.
Off: no moodle and no notice. The craving still builds, and you have to read it from irritability (the Angry moodle) and stress.
Sandbox_DanTraitsSmokerVanillaShown_tool:
Vitality has its own Smoker (+5): cravings by habit, withdrawal, damaged lungs and a cough, quit or relapse. The game's own Smoker (+3, tagged 'vanilla') is hidden on the creation screen.
On: both are offered; a character can take one or the other, never both.
Sandbox_DanTraitsInhalerLoot_tooltip:
How often inhalers turn up, in percent of the mod's normal rate. 100 is normal, 200 twice as often.
0: inhalers never spawn as loot (Asthma still starts with one).
Sandbox_DanTraitsInsulinLoot_tooltip:
How often insulin pens, insulin vials and insulin syringes turn up, in percent of the mod's normal rate. 100 is normal, 200 twice as often.
0: none spawn as loot. Insulin can still be made from an animal's pancreas (The Insulin Papers, or First Aid 8).
Sandbox_DanTraitsUntreatedDiabetesDays_t:
Blood sugar above 350 for more than two hours costs health, down to a floor. The floor then sinks, and is gone after this many days up there: 1 kills in about a day, 14 is a slow decline over two weeks. Time back under 350 wins the hours back.
0: never fatal. Health stops at 15%%.
Sandbox_DanTraitsKnoxSurviveChance_toolt:
The chance a Resilient character beats a zombie infection: a Run Down body (Vitality) has down to half of it. They get sick like anyone else, then the fever breaks partway through. Once only: a second infection is fatal within hours.
0: Resilient never survives it, as in the base game.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryEnabled_tooltip:
Washing and drying clothes take some care. Hand washing only gets clothes so clean (a washing machine gets them fully clean), wrung clothes stay damp, wet clothes dry slowly on the body and leave it a little stale, damp clothes left too long go musty, worn clothes go stale with sweat, old blood sets into a stain that needs bleach, and washing slowly wears fabric. Stale or musty clothes worn lower your mood a little.
Off: vanilla washing, wringing and drying; nothing on this page applies.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryHandFloor_toolti: How clean a hand wash without soap or cleaning liquid gets each patch of blood and dirt. 40: nothing comes out below 40%%. 0: fully clean, as in vanilla.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryHandSoapFloor_to: How clean a hand wash with soap or cleaning liquid gets each patch of blood and dirt. 0: fully clean, as in vanilla.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryBoardFloor_toolt: How clean a hand wash gets clothes when you carry a washboard, without soap. A washboard wash takes half as long again.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryBoardSoapFloor_t: How clean a hand wash gets clothes when you carry a washboard and soap or cleaning liquid.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryWringLeaves_tool: Wringing a garment out stops at this wetness (shoes at 70 or this, whichever is more). 10 is vanilla: wrung clothes are as good as dry.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryDampHours_toolti: How long a garment can stay damp (30%% wet or more) before it goes musty. Worn damp clothes count half as fast again. Musty clothes stay musty until washed.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryBodyDryRate_tool: How fast wet clothes dry while worn, in percent of the game's own speed. The game dries worn clothes very fast (a soaked shirt in about 20 minutes on a warm day); at 25 it takes about an hour and a half, longer in the cold. Every hour worn while damp also makes clothes a little stale. 100: as the game has it.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryOdourRate_toolti: How fast worn clothes go stale, in percent. Hard work and heat make them go faster; underwear, shirts, trousers and socks go fastest, jackets and hats at half the rate. 0: clothes never go stale from wear.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryMood_tooltip: How much what you wear moves your mood, in percent. Stale or musty clothes lower it a little, to a low cap; clean, dry, fresh clothes ease unhappiness and stress a little, twice as much when they were dried on a clothesline in daylight. 0: the moodle still shows but does nothing.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryStainDays_toolti: Days blood can sit on a garment before part of it sets into a stain. A stain stays through any wash until bleached out. 0: no stains.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryWear_tooltip: Each wash has a small chance to take a point of condition off a garment: hand washing least, a washboard and a washing machine more, bleach most. It never makes holes or goes below 1.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryClotheslines_too: Clothes hung on a clothesline dry with the weather: fast in sun, wind and warmth, slowly at night or in the cold, and rain soaks them again. Clotheslines can be built and the ones found in yards work too. Hanging in daylight also airs out a little staleness.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryLineDryRate_tool: How fast clothes dry on a clothesline, in percent.
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryPoncho: Garbage Bag Poncho and Fabric Protector
Sandbox_DanTraitsLaundryPoncho_tooltip: A garbage bag poncho can be made and worn over your clothes: it takes the blood and dirt for the parts it covers and tears as it is used. Fabric protector and fabric wax make a garment shrug off some of the blood and dirt and stay fresh longer, for a few washes.
Sandbox_DanTraitsReadingEnabled_tooltip:
Novels, comics, magazines and newspapers have a genre, a page count and a hidden quality. A read takes real time and its relief arrives per page; books are bookmarked by title. Each character likes one genre and dislikes another, found out by reading. Finishing a book gives the Good Read moodle with a buff set by the genre.
Off: reading works as in vanilla. Skill books and recipe magazines are vanilla either way.
Sandbox_DanTraitsReadingPageScale_toolti: Multiplies the time a page takes. At 1 a novel is 1.5 minutes a page and a comic or magazine half a minute, on top of the game's own Minutes Per Page option (2.0 is the default; a server that changes it changes this too). A 350-page novel is then about 9 hours, 6 with Fast Reader.
Sandbox_DanTraitsReadingRealBookChance_t: The chance, in percent, that a novel found in loot is a real book from before July 1993 (title and author only) instead of one of the game's own, from the same genre. 0 turns real books off.
Sandbox_DanTraitsReadingTasteStrength_to: How much a character's liked and disliked genres matter. At 1 a liked book does 25%% more and a disliked one half as much, both in the relief while reading and in the finishing moodle. 0 makes every genre the same; 2 doubles the difference.
Sandbox_DanTraitsReadingMoodleScale_tool: Multiplies how long the Good Read moodle and its genre buff last after finishing a book: at 1, two days for a novel, half a day for a comic or magazine.
Sandbox_DanTraitsReadingRereadComfort_to: A book you have finished still gives a fifth of its relief when it is in your liked genre: comfort reading. Off: a finished book gives nothing, as in vanilla. Other genres give nothing either way.
Sandbox_DanTraitsStrainEnabled_tooltip:
Fighting wears on you over days: kills (each costs more the more you have made since you slept), panic, wounds, bites, illness and withdrawal build burnout; sleep, calm hours, showers, fresh clothes, good meals, reading, workouts, a drink and a smoke ease it. Kills from a distance count less, and fighting wears on you less as your kills and days survived add up. Burnout slows the experience fighting gives (other skills a little, once it is high), never the fighting itself. Rested, combat experience is x1.1.
Off: nothing is tracked and the four burnout traits do nothing.
Sandbox_DanTraitsStrainGain_tooltip: Multiplies all burnout gained. 50 halves it, 200 doubles it.
Sandbox_DanTraitsStrainEase_tooltip: Multiplies everything that takes burnout off: sleep, calm hours, comforts, drink and smoke.
Sandbox_DanTraitsStrainXpFloor_tooltip: The least combat experience a burnt-out character still gets, as a share of normal. 100: burnout never slows experience.
Sandbox_DanTraitsStrainEarlyDays_tooltip: For this many days after the character starts, burnout builds slower (Burnout During Grace): the supply rush before there is a home to rest in. 0: no grace period.
Sandbox_DanTraitsStrainEarlyRate_tooltip: How much burnout counts during the grace days, as a share of normal. 50: half. 0: none at all until the grace days are over. 100: no grace.
Sandbox_DanTraitsStrainBreakdown_tooltip:
At full burnout the character breaks down at the first safe moment: sits down where they are for a while, then burnout drops to 60. Walking away or a zombie coming close stops it, and it comes again.
Off: full burnout only slows experience the most.
